svg.title: VHTR — The Scale Cascade
svg.text: A 950 °C VHTR resolved across six decades — one continuous zoom, left to right.
Every stage is the highlighted region of the one before it: 30 m of plot down to a 35 µm silicon-carbide shell — and the path the heat takes through all of it.
VHTR DESIGN PROJECT · MASTER SET · SHEET 2 OF 4
Preliminary design — every value is an estimate awaiting calculation. All values traced to design/00-summary.md and the linked sections.

g.text: warm air out — no plume, no steam
Scale by replication, not by size.
One helium loop, six states, no water
20 m of chimney height comes free with the excavation —
natural draught, no fan, no valve, no operator action.
THE BRAYTON RING — SIX STATES, ONE CLOSED LOOP
The manufacturing bet: a printed TPMS gyroid, not a drilled hole
≈ 20 gyroid unit cells across the block —
17.5 mm pitch, drawn at true density.
A triply periodic minimal surface splits the block into two interpenetrating
labyrinths — one helium, one graphite — with zero mean curvature everywhere.
No corners, no flow separation, maximum area per unit volume.
Nusselt number 20–40 % above a circular tube; j/f ratio 15–30 % better.
That surplus is what buys a 4 MPa primary circuit instead of 7 MPa.
